entities.name: PEGIDA
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
PEGIDA, or "Patriotic Europeans Against the Islamization of the West," emerged in Dresden, Germany, on October 20, 2014, as a far-right political movement. It arose during a period marked by rising anti-immigrant sentiment and fears regarding the impact of globalization and multiculturalism in Europe. The organization gained notoriety for its public demonstrations, which drew thousands of participants and sparked intense debates regarding national identity, immigration, and Islam's role in Europe, thus reflecting and amplifying a significant cultural and political divide within Western Europe.

In its early years, PEGIDA organized weekly protests that peaked with approximately 25,000 participants in January 2015, advocating against what they perceived as the Islamization of Europe. The group's rallies often featured controversial speakers and were met with counter-protests from anti-fascist and pro-immigrant groups. The movement's rise coincided with the European migrant crisis, which saw an influx of refugees and migrants into Europe, exacerbating existing tensions and prompting PEGIDA to frame their agenda as a defense of European Christian values and culture against perceived threats from Islam.

The legacy of PEGIDA can be seen in the broader rise of nationalist and populist movements across Europe and the world, contributing to the normalization of anti-immigrant rhetoric in political discourse. Its influence has led to the emergence of similar movements, such as France's National Rally and Italy's League, which have capitalized on fears surrounding immigration and cultural change. The organization has also prompted significant discussions regarding the limits of free speech and the role of protests in a democratic society, highlighting the ongoing struggles over national identity in an increasingly globalized world.
